transcript.text: Bosch SMS25AW00G, came back to E:09 on the display and the dishes are washed but stone cold. Is this an expensive fix?

It is difficult to say exactly how much it will cost without seeing the machine, but E:09 usually points to a heating circuit or flow-through heater issue which can be pricey if parts need replacing. Since your dishes are stone cold, this aligns with that code meaning there is likely no heat being generated during the wash. The most common causes for this are a faulty heater assembly, a failed temperature sensor, or sometimes just low rinse aid preventing proper drying and heat retention. To help narrow it down, please check if your rinse aid reservoir is full and set to at least level 3, as an empty tank can mimic heating problems. Then, try running a 65°C intensive programme with a normal load to see if the water gets hot this time or stays cold again.
I haven't checked the rinse aid, but both the hot programme and the eco one come out cold, so I don't think that's it. Would the heater be the expensive part to replace?

The heater assembly is often one of the more expensive parts to replace on these Bosch models, especially since it's integrated into the circulation pump rather than being a simple standalone element. However, before assuming the worst, we should rule out simpler issues like a faulty temperature sensor or wiring problems in the door hinge that can mimic a heater failure. The E:09 code typically indicates a flow-through heating element or circuit failure, which supports your observation of cold dishes. To help narrow this down, please check if the rinse aid level is low or empty, as this can sometimes affect how heat is retained during drying. Also, try running an intensive 65°C programme with a normal load to see if the water gets hot or stays cold throughout the cycle.

I already ran both the hot programme and eco and both came out cold. I haven't checked the rinse aid yet, so I don't know the level. Is there anything else I can test? I'm just trying to work out whether it's worth repairing a 9 year old machine.
AI service unavailable. Please try again in a moment.
Sorry, I think your last message didn't come through properly. Is there anything else I can test to tell whether the heater is the fault? I have a multimeter if that helps.

Since you have a multimeter, we can check if the heater is actually getting power, which helps tell if the fault is in the heating part or the control board. The E:09 code suggests a flow-through heating element failure, but it could also be the temperature sensor or wiring. First, make sure the dishwasher is switched off at the mains and unplugged for safety before you do anything. Then, locate the heater assembly (usually at the bottom of the tub) and use your multimeter to check if there is continuity across the heater terminals; a reading of around 20-30 ohms usually means it’s okay, while infinity suggests it has failed. If the heater tests fine, the issue might be the wiring loom in the door hinge or the control board not sending power to heat the water.

Ok, I'll unplug it and take the panel off and check across the heater terminals on the pump. I got an open circuit, no reading at all. Does that mean the heater has failed, and is that a costly repair on a 9 year old machine?

An open circuit reading across the heater terminals strongly suggests the flow-through heating element has indeed failed, which explains why your dishes are coming out cold and you're seeing the E:09 code. On a 9-year-old Bosch like yours, this repair can be moderately costly because the heater is often integrated into the circulation pump assembly, meaning you might need to replace both parts rather than just the heating element itself. While it’s not always the most expensive fix, given the age of the machine, it’s worth considering if a new unit would offer better energy efficiency and reliability. If you’re confident in your DIY skills, replacing the flow-through heater assembly is a manageable task for an experienced handyman, but if not, a qualified engineer will need to do it.
